title: U.S. House · Kansas's 4th District

context.text: Incumbent Ron Estes (R) defeated Frank McCollum in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Katy Tyndell won a four-candidate Democratic primary field. The 4th District drew the most candidates of any Kansas district in 2026 (six total). The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+12.

candidates.name: Ron Estes
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2017); previously Kansas State Treasurer (2011-2017) and Sedgwick County Treasurer (2005-2011)

summary.text: Ron Estes is the Republican incumbent representing Kansas's 4th District since 2017, succeeding Mike Pompeo. He previously served as Kansas State Treasurer and Sedgwick County Treasurer, and chairs the Social Security subcommittee of the House Ways and Means Committee.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in civil engineering and a master's degree in business administration from Tennessee Technological University.
Worked as a businessman and farmer before entering public office.
Served as Sedgwick County Treasurer (2005-2011) and Kansas State Treasurer (2011-2017).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, where he chairs the Social Security subcommittee and also sits on the Tax subcommittee; also serves on the Joint Economic Committee and the House Committee on Budget, 2025-2026 assignments.

candidates.name: Katy Tyndell

summary.text: Katy Tyndell is an attorney, business owner and civic leader with two decades of experience in independent oil and gas operations, small business, and public policy, running as the Democratic nominee on a platform of affordability and bipartisan problem-solving.

background.text: Describes herself as an attorney, business owner, civic leader and mother of three with deep Kansas roots.
Has spent about two decades in independent oil and gas operations, small business, and public policy, including federal government and non-profit advocacy experience.

priorities.text: Affordability: says tariffs are hurting Kansas farmers and wants policies that lower costs, strengthen domestic production, and help family farms and small businesses.
Wants to reduce partisan division and have leaders judged on character and ideas rather than party.
Wants Congress to reassert its constitutional role of legislating and conducting oversight rather than deferring to the executive branch.

positions.summary: Says tariffs are limiting market access and increasing uncertainty for Kansas farmers.
positions.quote: Our farmers are being hit especially hard by tariffs that limit market access and increase uncertainty

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and background drawn from Tyndell's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response; no separate campaign website was fetched.

candidates.name: Drew Cranmer

summary.text: Drew Cranmer is a data engineer and small-business founder from Wichita running as the Libertarian Party candidate on a platform of restoring Congress's constitutional war and spending powers and devolving policy to the states.

background.text: Describes himself as a data engineer, small-business founder, husband and father from Wichita.

priorities.text: Opposes undeclared wars and executive military action without a congressional declaration of war, citing every U.S. conflict since 1941.
Wants a balanced federal budget, across-the-board spending reductions, and a full audit of the Federal Reserve.
Wants to return education, healthcare, land use, and law enforcement policy to states and localities under the Tenth Amendment.

candidates.researchNotes: Based only on his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response; he did not state a direct position on any fixed issue key. No independent campaign website was fetched.
